title: Isolation levels under real concurrency, and the serialisation failure

videos.script: Two people raise the price of the same product at the same moment. Each adds a hundred cents. {{two}} Both updates succeed. No error, no warning. And the price went up by a hundred, not two hundred. {{lost}} That is a lost update, and the default isolation level in PostgreSQL allows it. {{default}} This lesson makes it happen in two windows, and then makes it happen a few thousand times a second, so you can count what was lost. {{count}} Then you climb the levels. Read committed, where every statement sees the latest committed data. {{rc}} Repeatable read, where a transaction keeps one snapshot, and refuses to overwrite a change it never saw. {{rr}} Serializable, which catches the case the others miss: two transactions that each check a rule, and together break it. {{ser}} The higher levels do not wait their way out of a conflict. They fail one of the transactions, with an error the application has to expect. {{fail}} So the last part is a short program that retries, written whole, and what each level costs in throughput and in retries. {{retry}} By the end, an isolation level will read to you as a choice about which mistakes the database catches for you. {{title}}
